title: ～ことは～が — it is true that ～, but ～
summary: Repeats the same word to say 'I admit that, but there is a drawback.' The first half concedes a fact and the second half gives the contrast.

patterns.form: V辞書形／Aい・Aな／Nである＋ことは＋同じ語＋が
patterns.gloss: Same word repeated: X ことは X が

body.p: Repeat the same verb: 読めることは読めるが. For い-adjectives: おいしいことはおいしいが. For な-adjectives and nouns: 好きなことは好きだが.

The first half grants a fact; it is not emphasis. The second half adds 'but it is not perfect' or 'there is a problem.' It is natural when you want to concede the first point while voicing a reservation.

examples.ja: 漢字（かんじ）は読（よ）めることは読（よ）めるが、書（か）けない。
examples.romaji: Kanji wa yomeru koto wa yomeru ga, kakenai.
examples.tr: I can read kanji all right, but I can't write them.

examples.ja: この料理（りょうり）、おいしいことはおいしいが、少（すこ）し高（たか）い。
examples.romaji: Kono ryōri, oishii koto wa oishii ga, sukoshi takai.
examples.tr: This dish is tasty all right, but it's a little expensive.

examples.ja: 泳（およ）げることは泳（およ）げるが、あまり得意（とくい）ではない。
examples.romaji: Oyogeru koto wa oyogeru ga, amari tokui de wa nai.
examples.tr: I can swim, it's true, but I'm not very good at it.

pitfalls: Use the same word before and after; different words break the pattern.
The second half must be a contrast, not more of the same.
